subject: orthopaedics
title: Metabolic bone disease: porous, soft and Pagetoid

steps.tx: **Osteoporosis** means weak bone that fractures easily, and a **DEXA** T score of minus 2.5 or lower makes the diagnosis. The **FRAX** tool estimates the ten year fracture risk and guides the treatment threshold. Glucocorticoids cause rapid trabecular bone loss, so calcium, vitamin D, protein and exercise form the base of care. Bisphosphonates reduce fractures, while stopping denosumab suddenly can cause rebound vertebral fractures.
steps.say: The scan measures bone density and compares the result with a healthy young adult. A very low score confirms weak bone that can fracture after minor trauma. A risk calculator then estimates the chance of fracture over ten years. Steroid treatment removes trabecular bone quickly and deserves early preventive therapy. Calcium, vitamin D, protein and regular exercise support every drug treatment.

steps.tx: **Rickets** softens growing bone and causes wrist widening, craniotabes and a rachitic rosary at the ribs, as this image set shows. Older patients develop osteomalacia with **Looser zones**, which are pseudofractures that ache. Blood tests show low calcium and phosphate with high alkaline phosphatase in nutritional disease. Vitamin D and sunlight treat nutritional cases, while phosphate wasting disease needs specialist therapy and monitoring.
steps.say: The picture can show a child whose soft bones bend under normal body weight. Swollen wrists and beaded rib ends reveal disease at the growing ends of bone. Weak adult bone can develop painful lines that mimic true fractures. Blood tests confirm poor mineral supply and raised bone turnover in most cases. Replacing the missing vitamin restores hardness to the growing skeleton gradually.

vis.alt: A child with bowed legs and a rachitic rosary, next to an X-ray showing widened wrist growth plates and a Looser's zone.
vis.caption: Clinical and radiological signs of rickets and osteomalacia

steps.tx: In **hyperparathyroidism** excess hormone resorbs bone and raises blood calcium, causing stones, bones, groans and thrones. A brown tumour can swell the jaw, and the skull film shows a **salt and pepper** granular pattern. A **rugger jersey spine** shows striped vertebral endplates on the lateral film. Removing a single parathyroid adenoma cures most primary cases, but hungry bone can crash calcium after surgery.
steps.say: Excess parathyroid hormone pulls calcium out of bone and raises the blood level. Kidney stones, bone pain, abdominal upset and confusion form the classic symptom groups. Local bone swelling can mimic a tumour in the jaw or long bones. One overactive gland causes most primary cases and surgery cures that gland. Bone that suddenly rebuilds after surgery can lower blood calcium sharply.

steps.tx: This lateral skull film shows **salt and pepper** granular demineralisation with loss of cortical definition in primary **hyperparathyroidism**. Fine resorption across the calvarium creates the speckled pattern that examiners love to show. The image matters because it separates hormone driven bone loss from simple osteoporosis. For the exam, pair this skull sign with brown tumours, rugger jersey spine and high calcium with raised hormone levels.
steps.say: The side view of the skull shows a fine speckled pattern throughout the bone. Normal sharp layering of the skull tables has faded because bone resorption is active. Excess parathyroid hormone can drive this widespread loss of mineral from the skeleton. The picture gives a fast visual clue when calcium and hormone levels are high. Examiners value this sign because few other disorders produce the same appearance.

vis.alt: Lateral skull X ray shows granular demineralisation and cortical loss in hyperparathyroidism.
vis.caption: Skull salt and pepper change in hyperparathyroidism. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Paget disease** rebuilds bone in a chaotic mosaic pattern with thick cement lines that look like a jigsaw. The skull may enlarge so hats fit poorly, and deafness can follow bone growth near the ear. Blood tests show isolated high **alkaline phosphatase** with normal calcium in active disease. **Scurvy** differs clearly because vitamin C lack causes gum bleeding, corkscrew hairs and bleeding under the periosteum.
steps.say: Disordered rebuilding makes some bones thick, weak and deformed at the same time. Enlarging skull bone can change hat size and damage hearing over years. A single raised enzyme with normal calcium strongly suggests active disease in older adults. Potent bone suppressing treatment relieves pain and slows the abnormal rebuilding process. Lack of vitamin C instead causes bleeding gums and painful limb swelling.
